findings.claim: Georgia's total truck-related fatalities rose from 142 in 2013 to 257 in 2023 — an 81% increase (body bullet and Key Takeaways)
findings.currentValue: NHTSA, Traffic Safety Facts: Large Trucks, 2024 Data (DOT HS 813 816), Table 7: Georgia, 197 people killed in traffic crashes involving large trucks in 2024 — 24 large-truck occupants, 142 occupants of other vehicles, 31 nonoccupants (173 'other people'). Table 6: 189 large trucks in Georgia fatal crashes, 9.5% of all vehicles in fatal crashes.
findings.sourceName: NHTSA, Traffic Safety Facts 2024 Data: Large Trucks (DOT HS 813 816)
findings.note: 142/257/81% not reproducible. Local FARS tally (STATE 13, crashes with a vehicle BODY_TYP in 60-64,66,67,71,72,78,79): 2013 143 crashes/164 deaths; 2014 155 deaths; 2020 234; 2021 246; 2022 271; 2023 176 crashes/193 deaths; 2024 201 deaths (NHTSA's published 197 uses its own definition). Neither endpoint matches; 2023 was a fall from 2022, not a peak. Replace with the NHTSA 2024 state figure.
